To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we provide the first consistent interpretation of both surface rotation velocity and lithium abundance patterns observed for an homogeneous sample of turn-off and evolved stars of the M67 cluster.

1) the surface lithium content of TO stars is consistent with that of young solar twins, and 2) the lithium evolution in M67 is consistent with the predictions of stellar models that include rotation-induced mixing.

the lithium abundance in the atmospheres of evolved stars in the old open cluster M 67 follows the expected evolutionary pattern, that is the decrease of lithium with increasing effective temperature.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that the lithium evolution of low-mass stars in the open cluster M 67 is well reproduced by non standard stellar models, which take into account atomic diffusion, rotation-induced mixing, and magnetic fields.
the lithium evolution in M 67 can be understood in the frame of standard models with rotation-induced transport.
the lithium abundances in M 67 evolved stars can be explained by rotation-induced mixing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the lithium abundances of evolved low-mass stars are not only determined by atomic diffusion, as often assumed, but also by the rotation history.
the lithium abundance evolution is a direct consequence of the evolution of the rotation rate, which is itself the result of the evolution of stellar angular momentum.

the lithium depletion observed in low-mass evolved stars can be explained by the action of the rotation-induced transport processes in the stellar interior, in agreement with the results obtained by the asteroseismology of solar-like pulsating stars.
